hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are riding high with the team top of the Premier League and a 67% title probability, embracing the '1-0 to The Arsenal' pragmatism while dreaming of a dynasty. Global Gooners share cannon sightings from Venice to Ottawa, and even opposition fans grudgingly respect the Gunners' momentum. The only clouds are familiar worries about whether Ethan Nwaneri avoids the Reiss Nelson 'what if' trajectory.

daily.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment followed a U-shaped trajectory across the day: starting measured and analytically anxious (7/10), dipping to edgy stress midday as the women's side surrendered a 2-0 lead (5/10), then surging to defiant pride by evening after both teams secured top-spot wins (8/10). The constant threads are tactical obsession, refereeing paranoia, and a siege mentality that frames 'ugly' 1-0 victories as badges of honour rather than cause for comfort. The dominant shift is from internal hand-wringing to external defiance — fans feel vindicated by results but besieged by narratives. The winning mixed with stress is a thing. There is no comfort, only defiance. Same as it ever was. It seems that wins feel like survival. The overall sentiment is that Arsenal fans are never comfortable, even when winning. The vibe is defiant. The vibe score is 7. The vibe word is defiant.

weekly.summary: The week began in euphoric triumph after a historic Anfield victory that sent Arsenal top, but sentiment quickly volatilized — swinging from confident title-race dominance to transfer-market cynicism and squad-management anxiety by mid-week. A recovery followed as rivals faltered and Arsenal extended their lead to six points, yet the prevailing mood remained edgy: fans frame every win as survival, haunted by refereeing paranoia, injury fears, and a siege mentality that refuses comfort even in success.
